blocks.content: Longshore drift carries sediments parallel to the shoreline, continuously reshaping coastal landforms through wave action.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Swash carries sediment up the shore at an angle aligned with prevailing winds, while backwash pulls material straight down due to gravity.
Longshore drift (littoral drift) is the primary process by which sediments are transported parallel to the coastline.
Transportation by waves creates distinctive depositional coastal landforms including beaches, spits, bars, barrier islands, and tombolos.
Sediment size and wave energy determine whether material moves via traction, saltation, suspension, or solution.

rows: Combes and erodes material, wearing beaches down
Low frequency (6 to 8 waves per minute)
High frequency (10 to 14 waves per minute)

items: Understand the functional difference between constructive waves (strong swash, weak backwash) and destructive waves (weak swash, strong backwash).
Identify Tombolo as a depositional wave-transport feature connecting an offshore island to the mainland.
Remember that longshore drift direction is determined primarily by the direction of prevailing winds.
